label: synthetic
title: Face-swap: AI face pasted into a real photo
note: A real photo with a pasted-in face: our team's classic deepfake pipeline (landmarks, triangle warp, Poisson blend) put a GAN face of a person who does not exist onto it. Look for the ghost eyebrows and lips. Caught only because the pasted face is itself AI-made: in testing VERITAS caught just 2 of 9 swaps like this. Photo: COCO / Flickr 8133371246, CC BY-SA 2.0; the edit is ours, same licence.

label: authentic
title: Real talking video
note: NASA astronaut message from the International Space Station (public domain, cropped). One of the clips we used to set the video thresholds: a demonstration, not a test. The face-swap detector stays quiet on it (about 15/100).

label: synthetic
title: AI 'talking photo'
note: A StyleGAN face animated with a slow camera move, the way cheap scam videos are made. It never blinks. Same recipe as the clips we used to set the video thresholds: a demonstration, not a test. Watch the face-swap detector score it near 0: it only knows swaps, so the AI-face model has to catch this one.

note: A public-domain audiobook reading (LJ Speech) re-rendered by a HiFi-GAN neural vocoder (WaveFake dataset, CC BY-SA 4.0). VERITAS calls it authentic: proof that no detector is perfect.
